claims.text: A critical threshold of nanoscale precipitate coherency governs toughness retention in near-equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The proposed coherency threshold is jointly defined by precipitate size, spacing, and continuity of matrix–precipitate interfaces.
The critical precipitate-size threshold is approximately 20 nm.
Coherent precipitates smaller than approximately 20 nm facilitate uniform plastic deformation and crack blunting through favorable dislocation interactions.
Precipitate coarsening or loss of coherency produces stress concentrations and reduces toughness.
A solution-treated CoCrFeMnNi alloy can have a homogeneous, single-phase FCC matrix with minimal precipitation.
An as-sintered CoCrFeMnNi alloy can be assumed to have a homogeneous, single-phase FCC matrix with minimal precipitation.
Controlled aging can systematically tune precipitate size, spacing, and coherency in CoCrFeMnNi.
Aging at approximately 600–800 °C can maintain precipitates below approximately 20 nm while preserving interface coherency in near-equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Tailored heat treatments induce controlled precipitation in CoCrFeMnNi.
Coherent nanoscale precipitates distribute plastic strain uniformly and blunt crack tips, thereby enhancing toughness.
Coarsened or incoherent precipitates cause dislocation pile-ups and local stress concentrations, resulting in toughness degradation.
Samples containing highly coherent precipitates below the critical size will retain or improve fracture toughness relative to unaged material.
Samples containing coarsened or incoherent precipitates will have significantly lower toughness than the unaged baseline.
The mechanism is expected to apply under room-temperature and moderately elevated-temperature, service-relevant strain-rate testing.
Outside the specified processing and composition range, grain-boundary sliding or phase transformations may dominate deformation.
TEM, XRD, fracture-toughness testing, and tensile testing can be used to compare precipitate state with mechanical response.
Failure to observe a distinct correlation or threshold between precipitate coherency and toughness relative to the unaged baseline would falsify the proposed governing-threshold hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The stated conditions and boundary restrict the regime to precipitates ideally below 20 nm and maintaining coherency, while the falsification experiment deliberately requires coarser and partially incoherent states. It is therefore unclear whether the predicted toughness-loss branch lies inside or outside the claimed validity boundary.
